note: The extensive scenario atlas: every problem-statement feature, the named use cases, multi-turn context behaviour and adversarial boundaries. An expectation is about the OUTCOME, never a label: 'answered' means facts came back, 'declined' means the engine said what it could not do, 'asked' means it needed one more thing, 'conversation' means no source was read. A scenario whose honest outcome is a decline is marked so: a corpus that expects an answer to an unanswerable question teaches the wrong lesson. Runner: scripts/run_atlas.py against a freshly started workspace.

scenarios.q: What is the weather in Zzyzxville?
scenarios.why: The property is that the turn asks back AND names the place it could not find. The assertion used to be the literal phrase "could not find", which the answer stopped containing on 21 September when clarifications began to be written rather than templated - it now says "I couldn’t find a place called Zzyzxville". Naming the unfound place survives rephrasing; a contraction does not.
